caption: Fig. 1 Correlations among behavioural indicators and comparisons of groupings. The analysis included 126,000 players, with 42,000 each on the North American (NA), Western European (EUW) and Korean (KR) servers and 20 matches per player. Each indicator was adjusted for sampling tier, team position, game patch and match duration, then averaged across each player’s 20 matches. a, Pearson correlations after removal of regional means. Circle area is proportional to |r|, and colour indicates the signed correlation coefficient; negative correlations are additionally outlined. Indicators 1–3 represent maintenance, 4–12 team signalling, 13–17 performance references and 18 the vision-score diagnostic. ‘Fewer deaths’ denotes the reverse-scored death indicator. b, Mean absolute Pearson correlations within maintenance (M), within signalling (S) and between M and S in each region. Each point summarizes 3, 36 or 27 indicator pairs, respectively. c, Comparison of the observed groupings with other possible groupings. The horizontal axis shows the difference between within-group and between-group mean absolute correlations, Δ, with equal weights assigned to all indicator pairs. Black diamonds indicate the observed groupings, and grey distributions show the results for all possible assignments that preserve the number of indicators in each group. The maintenance and signalling groups contain three and nine indicators, respectively, giving 220 possible assignments. The three functional signalling groups contain three, two and four indicators, giving 1,260 possible assignments. Each grey distribution is scaled to its maximum frequency. P values are from one-sided exact label-permutation tests, with Holm adjustment across the two tests.

caption: Fig. 2 Regional patterns of overall information investment and individual pings. The sample included 126,000 players (42,000 per region), 2,519,994 player–match records and 2,240,349 unique matches. a, Player-level distributions of the overall score. Densities were estimated using all players and a common bandwidth. Boxes span the 25th–75th percentiles, central lines mark the 50th percentile and whiskers span the 5th–95th percentiles. Symbols show regional adjusted means with 95% confidence intervals. The displayed range includes 99.74%–99.83% of players in each region; full distributions are shown in Supplementary Fig. 2. b, Adjusted means and 95% confidence intervals for maintenance and signalling. c, Adjusted means and 95% confidence intervals for the nine ping types. In a–c, 95% confidence intervals for adjusted means were estimated from 1,000 player-level resamples stratified by region and tier. Estimates for each resample were calculated using a first-order approximation; see Methods for details. d, Proportion of player–match records in which each ping was used at least once. Circle area is proportional to this proportion, and numbers indicate percentages. e, Mean number of pings per 10 min among player–match records containing the corresponding ping, with 95% confidence intervals calculated using the delta method with clustering by player. Panels d and e show unadjusted occurrence proportions and conditional frequencies, respectively; panels c–e use the same ordering of ping types. NA, EUW and KR are shown in purple, grey and vermilion, respectively, with diamonds, squares and circles additionally distinguishing their point estimates. Some intervals are narrower than the symbols. The 12 comparisons involving the overall score and the two processes and the 27 comparisons of individual ping types were assessed using two-sided Wald tests, with Holm adjustment applied separately to each family (Table 1 and Supplementary Tables 4 and 6).

Mean frequencies were calculated after standardizing the three regions to a common tier and patch distribution. The two teams in each match were averaged with equal weights. Lines connect the midpoints of fixed one-minute intervals without additional smoothing. The final interval ended at the match-specific cut-off, and its frequency was calculated using the actual interval duration. Shaded bands show pointwise 95% confidence intervals for mean behavioural frequencies under the common tier and patch reference, calculated from the joint covariance of match records within strata, with reference weights held fixed. d, Adjusted probability of blue-team acquisition of the first subsequent neutral objective, plotted against the early maintenance difference. The horizontal axis shows the blue-minus-red maintenance score difference divided by the common SD; zero indicates equal maintenance scores for the two teams. Curves were estimated from a model including a region × maintenance interaction and adjusting for sampling tier, game patch and early game state, then standardized to a common reference distribution. Shaded bands show pointwise 95% confidence intervals calculated from the covariance of match-level estimating scores within strata. Symbols mark −1, 0 and +1 SD. Adjusted probability differences between −1 and +1 common SD are reported in the Results and Supplementary Table 14. Purple diamonds and solid lines, grey squares and dashed lines, and vermilion circles and dash-dotted lines represent NA, EUW and KR, respectively. Panels a–c use natural frequency units; d uses maintenance scores calculated with fixed scoring parameters. Holm adjustment was applied to the 90 minute-by-minute regional comparisons. caption: Supplementary Fig. 2 Full player distributions and regional quantile differences in process scores. Each region included 42,000 players, with 2,519,994 player–match records in total. Scores were adjusted using regressions including region, tier, position, patch and match duration to a common reference with equal weights across the seven tiers and, separately, across the five positions, common patch proportions and mean match duration, then averaged within players. Solid lines represent maintenance and dashed lines signalling; symbols mark the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles. Curves use the 1st–99th percentiles within each region, with linear interpolation and no additional smoothing; the three panels share the same scales. All panels are descriptive and have no inferential intervals. The light-grey area in e marks the 96th–99th percentiles, where the KR–EUW signalling quantile difference is negative. In a–c, NA, EUW and KR are shown in purple, grey and vermilion, with solid, dashed and dash-dotted lines, respectively. In d–f, solid and dashed lines denote maintenance and signalling, respectively.

Supplementary Fig. 4 Regional contrasts in minute-by-minute maintenance frequencies. Columns show valid ward placement, valid ward clearing and control ward purchases, respectively; rows show KR–NA, KR–EUW and EUW–NA, respectively. Each retained tier × patch stratum contained at least 30 matches in each of the three regions. Intervals ran from [0,1] min and (1,2] min through (9 min, t*], where t* is the timestamp of the actual state frame near 10 min; frequencies in the final interval were calculated using its actual duration. Points show differences in mean frequencies under the common reference. Inner dark shading indicates pointwise 95% confidence intervals, and outer light shading indicates Bonferroni simultaneous 95% confidence intervals covering all 90 contrasts (three regional contrasts × three components × ten intervals). Shading is linearly connected across time points and does not represent a continuous-time confidence band; the zero line indicates no regional mean difference. Holm-adjusted P values from two-sided normal-approximation tests are provided in Supplementary Table 13b.

caption: Supplementary Fig. 5 Early maintenance across tiers under a common patch reference and tier-specific objective associations. a, Tier-specific means of maintenance scores during the first 10 min in NA, EUW and KR. Lines in a connect tier categories; points in b are not connected. Samples are defined separately for the two panels. NA, EUW and KR are represented by purple diamonds, grey squares and vermilion circles, respectively; where regional curves are drawn, they use solid, dashed and dash-dotted lines, respectively. Ir, Br, Si, Go, Pl, Em and Di denote Iron, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Emerald and Diamond, respectively.
